Definition: from G4862 and G2597; to descend in company with:--go down with.
BiblicalUsage: Festus tells the Jews that those among them who are able should go down with him to Caesarea and accuse Paul if there is any wickedness in him. Going down with the governor to accuse an innocent man is the business of a court, and the word is as plain as the deed.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that courts can be used against the innocent, and I hold that going down with accusers is a road I must not walk.
